request.description: Train the current baseline PPO recipe unchanged on its configured 0.14-0.20 m target-radius exposure, preserving the complete candidate checkpoints and runtime artifacts for subsequent official-like diagnostics.
request.rationale: No candidate or behavioral evidence exists yet. This baseline establishes a concrete reference under the existing implementation; its official-like performance and radius-stratified hold diagnostics will distinguish missing inner-radius coverage from a more general reach-and-stabilize limitation before changing the method.

request.description: Evaluate T1:checkpoint-115712 on the 160-episode official-like development panel with the scenario's radius, reach, hold, interruption, and final-distance diagnostics.
request.rationale: This checkpoint has a high training proxy without treating the terminal checkpoint as privileged. The broader evaluation distribution and episode diagnostics directly test whether the baseline gap is concentrated in inner-radius coverage, first reaching the tolerance, or maintaining the uninterrupted hold.

request.reason: This is the first complete learned artifact measured under the official-like distribution. It is the current working reference for diagnosing the 34.375 percentage-point gap; its diagnostics show 49/160 never reached tolerance and only 6/160 reached without completing the hold.

request.candidates_and_roles: Working: T1:checkpoint-115712, selected as the first complete artifact measured on the official-like panel (M1, 65.625%). Best-known: none; official assessment not justified. No retained candidates.
request.cumulative_resource_use: One fresh training run T1 requested 120000 steps and completed 120832 steps after rollout-boundary rounding; one 160-episode research evaluation M1; one working-role assignment E1. No official assessment or protected benchmark evidence was used.
request.current_goal_gap: The working baseline achieves 65.625% (105/160) on an official-like development panel, leaving 34.375 percentage points to the 98% goal. The gap is not yet attributable to a single mechanism: 49 episodes never entered tolerance, while 6 entered but failed to complete the hold; radius/angle stratification, branch selection, and action/substep dynamics are not yet measured.
request.current_synthesis: Observed: T1 trained the unchanged PPO 64-64 tanh recipe on the narrower 0.14-0.20 m training exposure; its training proxy rose to about 0.96 by 115712 steps. M1 measured the nonterminal checkpoint T1:checkpoint-115712 on 160 official-like episodes and recorded 105 successes. The 105 successes exactly match episodes with max_held_steps=100. Of the 55 failures, 49 had max_held_steps=0, so the dominant observed failure mode is failure to reach; six reached tolerance but did not sustain the required hold, showing a secondary stabilization problem. Interpretation: this supports the model's prediction that the exposure mismatch is consequential and makes broader target coverage the leading intervention hypothesis. Competing explanations remain branch/path selection, angle-conditioned transients, and sampled-data braking/conditioning; the visible catastrophic misses at inner radii and some angles are consistent with these alternatives but do not distinguish them. The baseline result is recipe- and runtime-specific: training proxies came from the narrow training distribution, and M1 contains no joint branch, action, or substep trajectory traces and no precomputed radius bins.
request.decision_frontier: The unresolved distinction is whether the 49 never-reached episodes are primarily caused by missing inner-radius exposure, or whether official-radius exposure alone will leave a consequential branch/angle/path-control failure requiring a branch-aware or stabilization redesign. A same-runtime comparison trained over the official radius range, evaluated on the same official-like panel with radius- and angle-stratified reach/hold diagnostics, would test the coverage hypothesis; joint/branch and action/substep traces would discriminate residual geometric-path failures from braking or sampled-dynamics failures. A large reach improvement with residual structured misses would redirect the campaign to that residual mechanism.
request.human_goal_connection: The human goal is at least 98% success on the official 0.06-0.20 m target distribution with an uninterrupted 100-control-step hold. This startup work establishes the first learned reference and identifies the dominant observed gap so the next inquiry can target the shortest credible route to that episode-level objective.
request.next_direction_or_closure: Enter goal review with the recorded frontier. If further bounded work is justified, open an inquiry on exposure versus residual branch/control failure and first compare a full-radius training implementation against the unchanged working baseline under matched official-like evaluation. Preserve the current baseline diagnostics as the reference rather than treating the training proxy as development success.
request.next_question: Which causal capability should drive the next intervention toward 98% official success: extending learning exposure to the full official radius range, or redesigning branch/path and stabilization control because the baseline's reach misses persist after exposure is corrected?

request.reason: T1:checkpoint-115712 is the only complete candidate measured on the official-like development panel. M1 records 105/160 successes (65.625%), with all successes completing the 100-step hold and 49/55 failures never reaching tolerance. This makes it the strongest evidence-backed candidate currently available, but far below the 98% goal and not a basis for claiming goal attainment.

request.closure_condition: Obtain and interpret a same-runtime full-official-radius candidate versus T1:checkpoint-115712 on matched official-like episode seeds, with radius- and angle-stratified first reach, minimum/final distance, maximum hold, interruptions, and success diagnostics. Close when these results establish that broader exposure materially changes the dominant no-reach failures, establish that it does not and leave a consequential structured residual requiring branch/path or stabilization work, or remain inconclusive with the unresolved distinction explicitly carried into the next goal review.
request.goal_connection: The current best-known candidate reaches only 105 of 160 official-like episodes (65.625%), leaving a 34.375 percentage-point gap to the 98% episode-success objective. Resolving whether missing inner-radius capability or residual branch/path and stabilization control is the dominant actionable limitation determines whether the next learned policy should first broaden exposure or redesign the closed-loop controller.
request.question: Which causal capability should drive the next intervention toward 98% official success: extending learning exposure to the full official radius range, or redesigning branch/path and stabilization control because the baseline's reach misses persist after exposure is corrected?
request.rationale: The baseline result is decisively below the goal, so requesting the terminal official assessment has poor expected value relative to one bounded causal intervention. The inherited coverage interpretation is supported but not established: M1 contains per-episode radius and angle fields, yet no matched full-radius candidate, branch/action traces, or substep dynamics. A full-radius comparison is the lowest-cost experiment that can test whether the 49 no-reach failures respond to exposure while preserving the current runtime and task semantics; structured residual reach or hold failures would redirect the campaign rather than justify attributing them to coverage.

request.current_goal_gap: The best-known development result is 65.625% (105/160), a 34.375 percentage-point gap to 98%. All 105 successes completed the full 100-step hold. Of 55 failures, 49 had max_held_steps=0 and six entered tolerance but failed to sustain it. The failure mechanism is not yet established.
request.current_synthesis: Observed: T1 used the unchanged PPO 64-64 tanh recipe with the baseline 0.14-0.20 m training exposure and completed 120832 steps; M1 evaluated T1:checkpoint-115712 on 160 official-like episodes and recorded 105 successes. The physical model predicts that official inner targets require greater folding while remaining nominally reachable, and that sampled-data braking and branch/path selection can affect reach and hold. Corrected inherited interpretation: M1 does preserve per-episode target_radius_cm and target_angle_degrees fields, so the evidence gap is not absence of target geometry; it is the lack of an explicit matched full-radius comparison and the lack of joint-branch, action, and substep trajectory traces. The existing result therefore supports, but does not establish, missing inner-radius exposure as the cause of the 49 no-reach failures. Competing explanations remain angle-conditioned transients from the common straight reset, branch/path selection and conditioning, and sampled-data braking or runtime-specific stabilization. The six reach-but-not-hold failures show that even a successful reach intervention may leave a consequential hold problem. The result is specific to the tested recipe, checkpoint, runtime, and evaluation panel; training proxies do not establish official-like performance.
request.decision_frontier: Determine whether broadening training exposure to 0.06-0.20 m materially removes the dominant no-reach failures, or whether substantial structured failures persist after exposure is corrected and therefore require branch/path or stabilization-control redesign. The discriminating evidence is a same-runtime full-official-radius candidate compared with T1:checkpoint-115712 on matched official-like episode seeds, with target-radius and angle stratification of first reach, minimum/final distance, maximum hold, interruptions, and success. Joint/action/substep traces remain unavailable in M1; if the matched comparison leaves structured residuals, those traces or an embodied dynamics measurement become consequential for the subsequent control decision.
request.human_goal_connection: The human goal is at least 98% success on the official 0.06-0.20 m target distribution with an uninterrupted 100-control-step hold. T1:checkpoint-115712 achieves 105/160 (65.625%) on the official-like development panel, so the next bounded work must identify the highest-leverage capability before committing the campaign to the terminal assessment.
request.next_direction_or_closure: Proceed with inquiry I1 rather than request the terminal official assessment. Train a same-runtime policy over the full official radius range, then compare it against T1 on matched official-like seeds and inspect radius/angle-separated reach and hold diagnostics. A large reduction in no-reach failures will support exposure as the next capability to develop; little or no reach improvement, or persistent structured angle/hold failures, will redirect the campaign toward branch/path and stabilization-control investigation. The official assessment remains premature because the only measured candidate is 65.625% and the causal choice can still be improved by this bounded comparison.

request.description: Train a fresh PPO 64-64 tanh policy with the unchanged baseline recipe and runtime, but expose the policy to the full official target-radius range of 0.06-0.20 m instead of the baseline's 0.14-0.20 m range.
request.rationale: This is the direct exposure intervention required by inquiry I1. The baseline T1/M1 result is 105/160 successes with 49 no-reach failures on the broader official-like distribution, but that observation does not establish missing inner-radius exposure as the cause because branch/path selection, fixed-start transients, and sampled-data stabilization remain alternatives. A same-runtime candidate trained over the full radius range supplies the decisive artifact-level comparison: if its matched-panel no-reach failures fall materially and the improvement is concentrated at inner radii, exposure becomes the next capability to develop; if substantial structured reach or hold failures persist, the campaign should redirect to branch/path and stabilization-control investigation. The full maintainer allocation is used because the inquiry contract requires 120000 steps, while preserving the PPO recipe and evaluation semantics makes the candidate's additional difference the training exposure.

request.description: Measure the step-matched full-radius candidate T2:checkpoint-115712 and the baseline T1:checkpoint-115712 on the same 160-episode official-like development panel, preserving radius- and angle-conditioned reach and hold diagnostics for the inquiry comparison.
request.rationale: This is the discriminating matched comparison for I1. T2 changes the training exposure from 0.14-0.20 m to the full 0.06-0.20 m range while preserving the PPO recipe, task mechanics, evaluation semantics, and runtime; selecting the 115712-step checkpoint also matches the measured T1 training duration rather than confounding exposure with extra optimization. Re-running T1 on the identical seeds establishes a same-runtime paired reference in this operation. The decision-relevant outcomes are success, first tolerance reach, minimum and final distance, maximum held steps, in-tolerance steps, and hold interruptions stratified by target radius and angle: an inner-radius reduction in no-reach failures supports exposure as the next capability, while persistent structured reach or hold failures redirects work toward branch/path and sampled-data stabilization control. Aggregate success alone will not establish the mechanism.

request.description: Compute deterministic radius- and angle-stratified reach/hold summaries and paired success transitions for the matched M2 baseline and full-radius evaluation artifacts.
request.rationale: M2 establishes that the tested full-radius exposure candidate is substantially worse overall, but the inquiry closure requires structured diagnostics to distinguish a broad reach/control degradation from a narrow inner-radius effect and to quantify residual hold failures. This PI-owned analysis consumes only the completed M2 artifacts, verifies matched episode geometry and panel identity, and reports the required reach, no-reach, hold, interruption, and paired transition metrics by fixed radius and angle strata. It does not alter the evaluation artifacts or claim causal proof; the result will determine whether I1 closes with a redirect toward branch/path and stabilization-control work.

request.outcome: I1 is resolved with a negative exposure result and a structured redirect. The step-matched full-radius candidate T2:checkpoint-115712 did not materially improve the dominant failure problem: on the matched 160-seed panel it achieved 73/160 (45.625%) versus T1:checkpoint-115712 at 105/160 (65.625%), a paired delta of -20.0 percentage points with 59 reference-success-to-candidate-failure transitions and 86 discordant episodes. M3 shows the residual is consequentially structured rather than a uniform inner-radius deficit: T2 improved [6,10) cm to 40.0% versus T1 22.5%, but scored 43.4% in [10,14), 53.8% in [14,18), and 46.4% in [18,20] versus T1 62.3%, 94.9%, and 92.9%; by angle T2 scored 100% in [-90,0) degrees and 0% in [90,180] degrees. T2 had 80 reaches and 80 no-reach failures, with 7 reached-but-not-success failures; T1 had 111 reaches, 49 no-reach failures, and 6 reached-but-not-success failures. The candidate also had 104 hold interruptions versus T1's 272, so the principal observed degradation is reach/path selection, with a consequential but smaller hold residual. The result establishes only the tested fresh PPO seed, checkpoint, runtime, and exposure implementation; it does not prove a universal causal effect of radius exposure or identify the exact branch/dynamics mechanism.
request.reason: The closure condition is met: a same-runtime full-official-radius candidate was compared with T1 on matched seeds with radius- and angle-stratified reach and hold diagnostics. Broader exposure did not improve overall success or remove the dominant no-reach failures, and M3 identifies strong angle- and radius-structured residuals requiring the next investigation to focus on branch/path selection and stabilization-control behavior. The exact mechanism remains unresolved because M2/M3 contain no joint-branch, action, or substep trajectories; those unknowns are carried into the next goal review rather than treated as settled.

request.candidates_and_roles: Working: T1:checkpoint-115712. Best-known: T1:checkpoint-115712, supported by M1 and re-confirmed in the matched baseline arm of M2; T2:checkpoint-115712 is not promoted because M2 measured 45.625% and M3 showed severe angle-structured failures. Retained: none. T2 remains an important negative comparison artifact, not a goal-certified model.
request.cumulative_resource_use: Before I1: one fresh baseline PPO training run T1 requested 120000 steps and completed 120832, one 160-episode M1 development evaluation, one best-known role assignment, and inquiry I1 opening. During I1: one fresh full-radius PPO run T2 requested 120000 steps and completed through the 120832-step checkpoint set; M2 evaluated T1 and T2 on two matched 160-episode panels (320 research-evaluation episodes total); M3 executed one PI-owned diagnostic analysis over those artifacts; I1 was closed as E6. No official assessment or protected benchmark evidence was consumed.
request.current_goal_gap: Best-known development performance is 105/160 = 65.625% for T1:checkpoint-115712, versus the 98% objective; the remaining gap is 34.375 percentage points. T2:checkpoint-115712 achieved 73/160 = 45.625% on the same matched panel and is not best-known. No protected official assessment has been requested.
request.current_synthesis: Established observations: T1 used the baseline 0.14-0.20 m training exposure and M1 recorded 105/160 successes, with 49 no-reach failures and six reached-but-not-held failures. T2 changed only the PI-owned training radius exposure to 0.06-0.20 m while retaining the PPO 64-64 tanh recipe, shared task mechanics, evaluation semantics, and runtime; its step-matched M2 comparison on the same 160 seeds recorded 73/160 versus T1's 105/160, -20.0 percentage points, 59 reference-success-to-candidate-failure transitions, and 86 discordant episodes. M3 established the structured pattern: T2 improved the [6,10) cm bin to 40.0% versus T1's 22.5%, but fell to 43.4%, 53.8%, and 46.4% in [10,14), [14,18), and [18,20] cm versus T1's 62.3%, 94.9%, and 92.9%; by angle T2 scored 100% in [-90,0) degrees and 0% in [90,180] degrees, while T1 scored 48.4% and 92.1% in those sectors. T2 had 80 reached episodes and 80 no-reach failures, with seven reached-but-not-success failures; T1 had 111 reaches, 49 no-reach failures, and six reached-but-not-success failures. T2 had fewer total hold interruptions (104 versus 272), so the dominant observed difference is reach/path behavior, although post-reach hold loss remains consequential. Interpretation and limits: broader exposure did not improve this tested candidate and leaves a strong angle/radius-structured residual consistent with branch/path selection or conditioning problems; it does not establish that exposure universally harms performance because T1 and T2 are different fresh training artifacts and the comparison has no joint, action, or substep traces. The exact branch and sampled-data dynamics mechanisms remain unresolved. The physical model's reachability claim remains plausible but is not a substitute for trajectory evidence.
request.decision_frontier: The exposure-vs-redesign distinction is resolved for the tested implementation: simply broadening exposure is not the next supported direction, because the full-radius candidate was substantially worse and retained structured no-reach failures. The next consequential distinction is whether T2's angle-specific failures arise primarily from inconsistent IK branch/path selection and fixed-start transient conditioning, or from sampled-data action/braking and post-reach stabilization. M2 and M3 cannot distinguish these causes because evaluation artifacts contain no joint trajectories, branch identity, actions, or MuJoCo substep distances. Evidence that would revise the direction is a matched candidate or diagnostic trace showing branch-consistent joint paths and action/substep behavior by angle/radius; persistent no-reach failures with branch/path divergence would favor branch-aware path redesign, while successful reach followed by boundary excursions or action sign/saturation patterns would favor stabilization-control redesign.
request.human_goal_connection: The human goal remains at least 98% success on the official 0.06-0.20 m radius and full-angle distribution with an uninterrupted 100-step hold. The best evidence-backed candidate remains T1:checkpoint-115712 at 105/160 (65.625%) on the official-like development panel, 32.375 percentage points below the goal; the new full-radius candidate is worse at 73/160 (45.625%), so the campaign is not ready for official assessment.
request.next_direction_or_closure: I1 is closed with a negative exposure result. Return to goal review with the next proposed question focused on discriminating branch/path selection from sampled-data stabilization. The campaign should not request the terminal official assessment: the best-known policy is 65.625%, and the new candidate is worse. The next bounded work should first obtain joint/IK-branch, action, and substep trajectory evidence or an embodied dynamics diagnostic, then choose a branch-aware or stabilization-control intervention based on that evidence.
request.next_question: Which branch/path and sampled-data stabilization mechanism should drive the next intervention toward 98% official success: angle-conditioned branch/path selection errors from the common straight reset, or post-reach braking and hold instability at the 50 Hz policy update rate?
